text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi Press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nine delegates to the secret tripartite meeting held in the Malawi capital Lilongwe to end the country's parliamentary boycott by opposition parties yielded no results after a seven-hour non-stop discussion.

- President Bakili Muluzi on Thursday pleaded with the opposition parties to end their parliamentary boycot, saying the National Assembly was the only forum where government and opposition can discuss issues of national interest.
- Three political parties locked horns in parliament on Thursday during serious discussions held in camera but refused to talk to reporters after adjouring seven hours later.

- President Bakili Muluzi's scheduled address to parliament next week may not take place if the High Court in Blantyre grants an injunction on Friday, applied for by ex-minister and independent member of parliament Rolf Patel and the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) to restrain next month's budget session in Zomba.

- Tea growers in Mulanje district have agreed to ground newly appointed Malawi High Commissioner to South Africa, John Chikago, a former Chief Executive for Malawi Tea Company, by seeking a court injunction until the wrangle between them is resolved.

- The Blantyre-based country's biggest referral hospital, Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, may have to close its only two paying wards unless the serious problem of staff shortages is resolved in the next seven days.
